newsitem.title: FIJI: Fiji sugar strike comes as crush proceeds well.
newsitem.headline: Fiji sugar strike comes as crush proceeds well.

text.p: The Fiji sugar workers strike, reported earlier on Monday, has come as crushing of the 1997 sugarcane crop was proceeding well on schedule and as sugar content of cane maintained good levels, Fiji Sugar Corp (FSC) managing director Jonetani Galuinadi said.
In a statement issued soon before the strike was called, he said the sugar content of cane presently averaged about 12 percent, about two percentage units better than a year earlier.
"We should be taking advantage of this POCS (sugar content) level by crushing more cane and maximising production of good quality sugar," he said in the statement.

To Friday July 18, FSC's four mills had crushed a total of 651,000 tonnes of cane and produced 67,000 tonnes of raw sugar. This was ahead of the 626,000 tonnes of cane crushed and 56,000 tonnes of sugar produded in the same period of last year, Galuinadi said.
Fiji produced 475,000 tonnes of raw sugar in 1996 but its canefields were hit by cyclone Gavin in March.
Cane burning was rising and last week averaged about five percent of the total crush, more than the one percent of cane burnt at this time last season, Galuinadi said in the statement.
"To meet sugar production targets for 1997, everyone in the industry must now continue to work together and maintain what so far has been a good season," he said in the statement.
Members of the Fiji Sugar and General Worker Union started their strike on Monday morning, seeking a 3.5 percent pay rise.
FSC has said it cannot afford to meet the demand. This position has been backed by the Sugar Tribunal.
